glosses: A tabular schedule of events with the times at which they occur, especially times of arrivals and departures.

examples.text: The timetable has been changed several times since it was first announced.

glosses: A schedule of arrivals and departures published in book or booklet form, or as a pamphlet, and available to travellers, either free or for a charge.

examples.text: Above all, the 48-page timetables of the new service, which have been distributed free at every station in the scheme, are a model to the rest of B.R. For the first time on British Railways, so far as we are aware, a substantial timetable has been produced, not only without a single footnote but also devoid of all wearisome asterisks, stars, letter suffixes and other hieroglyphics.

glosses: To arrange a specific time for (an event, a class, etc).

examples.text: I've timetabled the meeting for Monday afternoon.

translations.source_sense_description: Übersicht über die Fahrzeiten eines Verkehrsmittels

glosses: A procedural plan, usually but not necessarily tabular in nature, indicating a sequence of operations and the planned times at which those operations are to occur.

examples.text: To complete on time, we must follow the schedule.

glosses: A serial record of items, systematically arranged.
A written or printed table of information, often forming an annex or appendix to a statute or other regulatory instrument, or to a legal contract.

examples.text: schedule of tribes

glosses: A written or printed table of information, often forming an annex or appendix to a statute or other regulatory instrument, or to a legal contract.
One of the five divisions into which controlled substances are classified, or the restrictions denoted by such classification.

examples.text: Heroin is a Schedule I drug with a high potential for abuse.

Currently, cannabis/marijuana is classified as a Schedule I drug, meaning it defined as having “no currently accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse.” This is the same designation given to LSD, heroin and ecstasy.

glosses: A written or printed table of information, often forming an annex or appendix to a statute or other regulatory instrument, or to a legal contract.

An allocation or ordering of a set of tasks on one or several resources.

examples.text: He demands the blood-written schedule back from the demon, who refuses to give it up

glosses: To create a time-schedule.
To plan (an activity or event) for a specific date or time.

examples.text: The next elections are scheduled on the twentieth of November.

glosses: To add (a name) to the list of those participating in an event; to reserve a place or time for.

examples.text: I am scheduled for classes next month.

examples.text: Many harm reduction groups and drug policy experts question the long-term efficacy of scheduling xylazine.

glosses: Qui se produit à chaque heure.
Qui tourne comme les aiguilles d’une montre.

examples.text: Puis trois fibres, ainsi créées, sont rassemblées et tissées ensemble dans le sens horaire pour former la corde.

glosses: Indicateur des heures d'ouverture et de fermeture d'un service, des heures de départ et et d’arrivée des trains, des avions ou autres opérateurs de transport.

examples.text: Je me suis procuré un horaire et je le consulte. La carte dont il est accompagné me fait connaître, station par station, le parcours du railway entre Tiflis et Bakou.
Je suis habitué à ces fantaisies d’officiers. À la caserne, on est fréquemment convoqué par un capitaine inconnu qui veut connaître sans délai l’horaire de paquebots pour la Chine.

glosses: Répartition des heures d’occupation, de travail d’une ou plusieurs personnes.

examples.text: Je n’ai point consulté mon horaire.
